heading: Learn Korean, from Hangul to TOPIK 6.
lead: A complete course in standard South Korean for English speakers, from the alphabet to advanced Korean: 80 modules in eight tiers that follow the grammar of TOPIK 1 to 6. The speech levels and honorifics are taught in order, the grammar is explained directly, and every exercise tells you why an answer is right or wrong.
fineprint: The whole course, the grammar reference and word practice are free. Specializations, TOPIK practice papers, conversation practice and the other extras are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year.

panel.label: The course, tier by tier

items.title: 1 · Hangul and sounds
items.text: The alphabet, syllable blocks, final consonants, sound changes, typing Hangul.

items.title: 2 · Everyday basics
items.text: Both number systems and counters, polite verbs, the past tense, adjectives.

items.title: 3 · Daily life
items.text: Requests and suggestions, negation, joining clauses, the future, shopping.

items.title: 4 · Building sentences
items.text: The formal polite style, honorifics, casual speech, noun-modifying clauses.

items.title: 5 · Building fluency
items.text: Nominalisation, conjecture, reported speech, the written style, conditions.

items.title: 6 · Intermediate
items.text: The passive and causative, the retrospective, concession, hypothesis and regret.

items.title: 7 · Upper intermediate
items.text: Business Korean, formal connectives, Sino-Korean words, the news, official Korean.

items.title: 8 · Advanced
items.text: Literary grammar, older speech levels, idioms, spoken Korean, dialects, literature.

panel.note: 80 modules in eight tiers that follow TOPIK 1 to 6, plus 13 professional specializations with 117 more modules.

sections.heading: What the course teaches, and how

items.title: Hangul first
items.text: The first tier teaches the alphabet, syllable blocks, final consonants (받침) and the sound changes, and you type on the standard two-set keyboard from the start, with an on-screen jamo keyboard.

items.title: Speech levels in order
items.text: The polite 해요체 comes first, then the formal 합니다체, honorifics and casual speech in Tier 4, the written 한다체 in Tier 5, and older and literary forms in Tier 8, so you know which ending fits whom.

items.title: The grammar taught directly
items.text: Particles, connectives, noun-modifying clauses, reported speech, the passive and causative and the endings of conjecture each have their own modules, explained in plain English with examples.

items.title: Feedback that says why
items.text: Every answer gets feedback with a reason and a link to the grammar rule behind it. Every Korean word can be tapped for its meaning, forms, an example and audio.

items.title: Pronunciation feedback
items.text: Speaking exercises assess your pronunciation of Korean sentences word by word.

items.title: Common traps
items.text: Twelve short sets on the mistakes English speakers make, such as 은/는 against 이/가, 안 against 못, the two number systems, word spacing and Konglish.

sections.heading: Practice papers for TOPIK
sections.intro: The course has timed practice papers for both tests of the Test of Proficiency in Korean (한국어능력시험), in the paper-based test's task types and with original content. Neither covers the separate speaking test. What the papers cover and how they differ from the real test.
items: TOPIK I, levels 1 and 2: two full-length papers of listening and reading, for learners who have finished Tier 4.
TOPIK II, levels 3 to 6: two papers of listening, writing and reading, for learners who have finished Tier 6; the hardest items assume Tier 8.

sections.heading: Korean for your field
sections.intro: Thirteen specialization courses, nine modules each, in three stages: Foundations after Tier 3, Working vocabulary after Tier 5 and Professional after Tier 7. Each teaches the vocabulary and register of one field.

items.question: Do I need to know Hangul before I start?
items.answer: No. The first tier starts with the vowels and the first consonants, then syllable blocks, final consonants and the sound changes, and you learn to type Hangul as you go.

items.question: Which Korean does the course teach?
items.answer: Standard South Korean, based on the speech of Seoul. Tier 8 also has a module on the dialects and on North Korean usage.

items.question: Does the course prepare me for TOPIK?
items.answer: The tiers follow the grammar of TOPIK 1 to 6, and Premium has two timed practice papers each for TOPIK I and TOPIK II. The papers show the share of points you got, not a TOPIK level, and no course can promise a result.

items.question: Is the Korean course really free?
items.answer: Yes. All 80 modules, the grammar reference, word practice, the placement test and 5 Ask AI questions a day are free. The TOPIK papers, specializations, stories, conversation practice and the other extras are part of Premium.

items.question: Can I practise speaking?
items.answer: The course's speaking exercises give feedback on your pronunciation word by word. With Premium you can also hold typed or spoken conversations with an AI character in 38 situations, and practise pronunciation on sentences you type.

closing.heading: Start with Hangul, or wherever you are.
closing.text: Sign in with Google, take the placement test if you already know some Korean, and open the first module.
